summary: Implemented label-scoped, confirmation-gated app removal with default volume retention, optional labelled-volume deletion, foreign-volume refusal, image cleanup that protects shared/in-use images, lock-scoped orchestration, and a 22-test unit suite. Typecheck, lint, build, focused suites, and the full 785-test suite pass.

decisions: A non-TTY without --yes or --force exits 1 before the lock and before any Podman or filesystem call, so it cannot delete anything.
--force skips confirmation only and never implies --volumes.
Volumes are planned from an unfiltered listing and filtered by the io.easy-host.app label; a name-matching volume with a missing or foreign label is reported as refused, never deleted.

Images are candidates when labelled for the app or when the app's own state.json recorded that exact reference; the recorded-reference fallback exists because Railpack images are not labelled yet, and it is never tag-pattern matching.
Images used by another running container, recorded by another app, or labelled for another app are kept and reported.
Images and volumes are removed before the workspace and app directory; the app directory is deleted last so a failed step leaves a registered, retryable app.
App directory and workspace paths are asserted to be app-scoped before deletion; local-mode source is only removed as part of the app directory and never as a separate host path.
Retained volumes are reported with `podman volume rm <names>` because `easy-host remove` cannot run again after the app entry is gone.

payload.taskDescription: Implement remove.ts and the remove command. Acquire the lock, print the exact resources to be deleted, require --yes on a non-TTY, stop and delete the container, delete the workspace and app directory, delete retained images, and leave volumes unless --volumes is passed. With --volumes, list volumes by the app label and delete only those, reporting any unlabelled volume it refused to touch. Tests cover default removal, --volumes removal, non-TTY without --yes, lock contention, a foreign volume, and an already-absent container.
